band_or_state: Bands 1 & 2 (positive-parity MchiD pair) and Bands 3 & 4 (negative-parity MchiD pair) + interband E1 transitions
physical_mechanism: Multiple chiral doublet bands (MchiD) accompanied by dynamic octupole correlations
experimental_facility: iThemba LABS AFRODITE array (9 Compton-suppressed clover detectors + 8 LEPS)
lifetime_technique: None (no DSAM/RDDS lifetimes measured for these high-spin states; only relative branchings)
reduced_transition_probabilities: B(E1)/B(E2) branching ratios: 0.5(1) x 10^-5 to 2.2(4) x 10^-5 fm^-2 (Fig. 5, p. 4); no absolute B(E1), B(M1), or B(E2)
branching_and_angular_ratios: DCO ratios R_DCO = 0.50(5) - 0.70(7) for Delta I=1 transitions; linear polarization asymmetry Delta_IPLO > 0 confirming electric (E1) character of connecting transitions
citation_primary: C. Liu et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 116, 112501 (2016)
citation_locators: PRL 116, 112501: p. 2 Fig. 1 (level scheme), p. 3 Fig. 3 (spectra/polarization), p. 4 Fig. 4 (TPRM calculations), p. 4 Fig. 5 (B(E1)/B(E2) and delta E)
direct_experimental_observable: Prompt gamma-gamma coincidences, directional correlation from oriented states (DCO), and two-leaf clover Compton linear polarization asymmetry Delta_IPLO
derived_physical_quantity: Energy displacement delta E(I) = E(I-) - [E((I+1)+) + E((I-1)+)]/2 decreasing from ~300 keV to ~120 keV; S(I) staggering parameter; branching ratio B(E1)/B(E2)
model_dependent_interpretation: Authors interpret Bands 1-4 as two pairs of chiral doublet bands (MchiD) based on pi g9/2 (x) nu g9/2 (positive parity) and pi(f5/2/p3/2) (x) nu g9/2 (negative parity); E1 links interpreted as octupole correlations within triaxial particle-rotor model (TPRM)
competing_explanations_and_limits: Absence of absolute level lifetimes means true chiral B(E2) degeneracy cannot be confirmed; B(E1)/B(E2) is ~10 times smaller than in 224Th (stable octupole benchmark); non-zero delta E(I) proves octupole correlation is dynamic vibration/softness rather than static pear shape

band_or_state: Bands 1 & 2 (positive-parity chiral candidate doublet) + Band 3 (negative-parity octupole-correlated band)
physical_mechanism: Chiral candidate geometry competing with octupole vibration in Z=33 odd-odd nucleus
experimental_facility: iThemba LABS AFRODITE array (9 clover + 8 LEPS)
reduced_transition_probabilities: Branching B(M1)/B(E2) ~ 0.5 - 2.0 (mu_N/eb)^2; B(E1)/B(E2) ~ 0.8(2) x 10^-5 to 2.4(5) x 10^-5 fm^-2; no absolute strengths
branching_and_angular_ratios: 372.4 keV linking transition: R_ADO = 0.75(6), polarization asymmetry A_p = +0.06(5), establishing pure E1 multipolarity
citation_primary: X. Xiao et al., Phys. Rev. C 106, 064302 (2022)
citation_locators: PRC 106, 064302: p. 2 Table I (transitions & multipolarities), p. 3 Fig. 1 (level scheme), p. 6 Fig. 5 (S(I) and B(M1)/B(E2)), p. 7 Fig. 7 (B(E1)/B(E2) & delta E)
direct_experimental_observable: Gamma-gamma coincidence intensities, angular distribution ratios (ADO), and linear polarization asymmetry A_p
derived_physical_quantity: Multipole mixing ratio delta ~ 0 for linking lines; energy separation Delta E ~ 400 keV between Bands 1 and 2; energy displacement delta E(I) ~ 200-400 keV
model_dependent_interpretation: TPRM assigns Bands 1 & 2 as pi g9/2 (x) nu g9/2 chiral partner bands and Band 3 as octupole-coupled pi(f5/2/p3/2) (x) nu g9/2 configuration
competing_explanations_and_limits: Energy splitting of ~400 keV is substantial (far from degenerate); no level lifetimes; delta E(I) is positive and large, ruling out static octupole deformation and confirming soft vibrational correlations

physical_mechanism: Antimagnetic rotation (AMR, double shears mechanism without net transverse magnetic dipole)
experimental_facility: TIFR-BARC Pelletron Facility, Indian National Gamma Array (INGA) with 19 clover detectors
reaction: 96Zr(13C, 5n)104Pd at E_beam = 63 MeV; thick target with Au backing
lifetime_technique: Doppler-Shift Attenuation Method (DSAM) lineshape analysis across 7 detector angles (32 deg to 157 deg)
level_lifetimes_tau: DSAM sub-picosecond lifetimes: extracted level lifetimes decrease along cascade (tau ~ 0.5 to 0.1 ps)
citation_primary: N. Rather et al., Phys. Rev. C 89, 061303(R) (2014) / arXiv:1402.3422v1
citation_locators: PRC 89, 061303(R): p. 2 Fig. 1 (spectra), p. 3 Fig. 2 (DSAM fits), p. 4 Fig. 3 (B(E2) & J(2)), p. 5 Table 1 (lifetimes, B(E2), J(2)/B(E2))
direct_experimental_observable: Doppler-broadened gamma lineshapes at forward, backward, and 90-degree INGA clover detectors
derived_physical_quantity: Level lifetimes tau, reduced transition probabilities B(E2) in (e b)^2, dynamic moments of inertia J(2) = 29.2 to 63.5 hbar^2/MeV
model_dependent_interpretation: Semiclassical two-shears model: two g9/2 proton holes coupling to four h11/2 neutron particles; shears angle closes from 60 deg to 20 deg, driving B(E2) propto sin^4(theta)
competing_explanations_and_limits: High-spin neutron alignment at I=20+ creates a finite-difference peak in J(2); stopping-power database uncertainties (~15-20%) affect absolute tau; Zhang 2019 PNC-CSM calculation indicates 4 partial g9/2 holes rather than pure 2-hole effective model

band_or_state: Yrast Delta I = 2 cascade from 16+ to 24+
physical_mechanism: Antimagnetic rotation coupled with collective core rotation (two-shears + rotor)
experimental_facility: Inter-University Accelerator Centre (IUAC) New Delhi, 15-UD Pelletron, INGA array (18 clover detectors)
lifetime_technique: DSAM lineshape analysis using LINESHAPE code (Wells & Johnson)
branching_and_angular_ratios: Pure Delta I=2 cascade; no interband or in-band Delta I=1 transitions observed; DCO ratios R_DCO ~ 1.0 confirming stretched E2
citation_primary: S. Roy et al., Phys. Lett. B 694, 322 (2011)
citation_locators: PLB 694, 322: p. 323 Fig. 1 (scheme & spectra), p. 324 Table 1 (tau and B(E2)), p. 325 Fig. 3 (J(2) vs omega), p. 326 Fig. 4 (classical model fits)
direct_experimental_observable: DSAM Doppler profiles at angles 32, 57, 90, 123, 148 deg, measured with Compton-suppressed clover detectors
derived_physical_quantity: Level lifetimes tau (0.17 to 0.36 ps), absolute B(E2) values, J(2) dynamic inertia showing an 8 hbar alignment gain at hbar omega = 0.65-0.72 MeV
model_dependent_interpretation: Classical two-shears model with core participation: pi g9/2^-2 coupled to nu h11/2^2, core rotation inertia I_core = 19.5 MeV^-1 hbar^2 (about half the rigid-body value). Core rotation explains the gentle B(E2) plateau and why B(E2) doesn't plunge to zero as fast as in 106Cd
competing_explanations_and_limits: Low-spin 110Cd (0+ to 6+) is the classic textbook spherical quadrupole vibrator (U(5) symmetry); at high spin (I>=16+), breaks into AMR double shears. Transition from vibrator to AMR is a competition between core vibration and quasiparticle shears; 20% systematic stopping power uncertainty

band_or_state: Band 1 (yrast pi h11/2 decoupled band) and Band 2 (excited Delta I = 1 band; former transverse wobbler candidate)
physical_mechanism: Magnetic rotation (shears band) vs signature partner band; definitive experimental falsification of transverse wobbling
experimental_facility: LNL GASP array and TIFR INGA array
reaction: 120Sn(19F, 4n)135Pr at E_beam = 82 MeV (GASP) and 123Sb(16O, 4n)135Pr at 80 MeV (INGA)
lifetime_technique: Relative branchings + high-precision angular distribution and Compton polarimetry (no new lifetime required to rule out wobbling)
transition_energies_E_gamma_keV: 747.2 keV linking transition (17/2- Band 2 -> 15/2- Band 1); 594.1 keV (Band 2 in-band 17/2- -> 13/2-)
level_lifetimes_tau: tau ~ 1.0 - 3.0 ps (from earlier Matta 2015 DSAM / Santos 1997 RDDS)
reduced_transition_probabilities: Crucial ratio: B(E2)_out/B(E2)_in < 0.005 (e b)^2; B(M1)_out/B(E2)_in ~ 2.5 (mu_N/eb)^2. E2 strength is suppressed by >95% compared to wobbling prediction!
branching_and_angular_ratios: 747.2 keV transition: R_DCO = 0.52(2), Legendre coefficients A2 = -0.23(2), A4 = +0.01(2); linear polarization asymmetry Delta = +0.13(3), polarization P = -0.21(5). Unambiguously yields delta = -0.19(3) (96.5% M1, 3.5% E2), decisively ruling out delta = -4.7(6) (72% E2)
citation_primary: B.F. Lv et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 128, 242503 (2022); see also N. Sensharma et al., PRL 124, 052501 (2020) and M.A. Matta et al., PRL 114, 082501 (2015)
citation_locators: PRL 128, 242503: p. 2 Fig. 1 (level scheme), p. 3 Fig. 2 (DCO and polarization fits), p. 4 Fig. 3 (chi^2 vs delta), p. 4 Table I (extracted multipolarities)
direct_experimental_observable: Prompt coincidence gamma-ray intensities, directional correlation ratios R_DCO, Legendre angular distribution coefficients (A2, A4), and Compton linear polarization asymmetry Delta
derived_physical_quantity: Multipole mixing ratio delta = -0.19(3), multipole purity 96.5% M1 + 3.5% E2, B(M1)/B(E2) ratios
model_dependent_interpretation: Band 2 is re-assigned as a magnetic rotation (MR) shears band based on pi h11/2 (x) nu(h11/2^-1 d3/2^-1) or signature partner band; transverse wobbling phonon hypothesis is falsified
competing_explanations_and_limits: Landmark case showing how a false-positive wobbler was created in literature: Matta 2015 adopted delta = -1.6(2) without linear polarization, mistaking an M1 shears band for an E2 wobbler. Proves cross-mass transfer of wobbling criteria without polarization is invalid!

band_or_state: Yrast negative-parity band based on nu h11/2 (7/2-[523] Nilsson orbital)
physical_mechanism: Triaxial prolate-driven collective rotation; testing low-spin wobbling candidates vs signature partner bands
experimental_facility: LNL GASP array coupled with Cologne Plunger
lifetime_technique: Recoil Distance Doppler Shift (RDDS) method across 14 target-to-stopper distances (10 um to 3000 um)
branching_and_angular_ratios: Pure stretched E2 cascades; transition quadrupole moment Q_t = 3.8(3) e b (beta2 ~ 0.23, gamma ~ -15 to -20 deg)
citation_primary: B.S. Nara Singh et al., Phys. Rev. C 94, 054308 (2016); see also C.M. Petrache et al., PRC 57, R1011 (1998)
citation_locators: PRC 94, 054308: p. 2 Fig. 1 (spectra), p. 3 Fig. 2 (decay curves), p. 4 Table I (lifetimes, B(E2), Q_t), p. 5 Fig. 4 (Q_t vs spin)
direct_experimental_observable: Shifted and unshifted peak intensities as a function of target-to-stopper plunger displacement
derived_physical_quantity: Differential decay curve method (DDCM) level lifetimes tau (0.5 to 9.6 ps); absolute B(E2) transition strengths in (e b)^2; transition quadrupole moments Q_t
model_dependent_interpretation: Cranked Nilsson-Strutinsky and triaxial particle-rotor model: moderate triaxial prolate deformation driven by nu h11/2 quasi-neutron coupling
competing_explanations_and_limits: Demonstrates that putative wobbling bands in A~130 odd-N cerium isotopes lack the enhanced interband B(E2) observed in Lu; low-spin wobbling candidates are more naturally explained by signature partners or gamma-vibrations

physical_mechanism: Static nuclear chirality vs chiral vibration / shape coexistence in odd-odd nucleus
experimental_facility: EUROBALL IV and Cologne Plunger at IReS Strasbourg
lifetime_technique: Recoil Distance Doppler Shift (RDDS) method with strict gamma-gamma coincidence gating to eliminate unobserved side-feeding
transition_energies_E_gamma_keV: Band 1: 325, 404, 478, 553; Band 2: 378, 460, 544; connecting transitions between bands
branching_and_angular_ratios: B(M1)/B(E2) ratios identical between Bands 1 and 2 within experimental errors; DCO ratios confirm M1/E2 mixtures
citation_primary: E.O. Lieder et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 112, 202502 (2014); contradicting D. Tonev et al., PRL 96, 052501 (2006); original discovery K. Starosta et al., PRL 86, 971 (2001)
citation_locators: PRL 112, 202502: p. 2 Fig. 1 (gated spectra), p. 3 Fig. 2 (decay curves), p. 4 Fig. 3 (B(E2) and B(M1) comparison)
direct_experimental_observable: Gated decay curves measured at 18 plunger distances (8 um to 4000 um) using coincidence gates from above
derived_physical_quantity: Level lifetimes tau, absolute B(E2) and B(M1) values in both partner bands
model_dependent_interpretation: Rigid 3D chirality: pi h11/2 (x) nu h11/2 configuration mutually perpendicular to core rotational axis, creating degenerate left- and right-handed states
competing_explanations_and_limits: Crucial methodological lesson: Tonev 2006 had claimed B(E2) differed by a factor of 2 (arguing for chiral vibration); Lieder 2014 proved Tonev used singles/uncleaned gates contaminated by slow unobserved side-feeding. Demonstrates how RDDS systematic errors can fabricate false physics!

band_or_state: TSD1 (yrast, n_w=0) and TSD2 (n_w=1 wobbling phonon band) and TSD3 (n_w=2 wobbling band)
physical_mechanism: Transverse wobbling of a triaxial superdeformed (TSD) rotor coupled to an aligned i13/2 proton
experimental_facility: EUROBALL IV array at Vivitron accelerator, IReS Strasbourg (Compton-suppressed Ge + BGO inner ball)
lifetime_technique: DSAM and RDDS methods (Görgen 2001, Schönwasser 2003) measuring transition quadrupole moment Q_t
transition_energies_E_gamma_keV: Nine TSD2->TSD1 connecting transitions: e.g. 540 keV (43/2+->41/2+), 580 keV (47/2+->45/2+); in-band TSD1: 720-1100 keV
level_lifetimes_tau: High-spin lifetimes tau ~ 0.05 - 0.3 ps; measured Q_t = 10.7(7) e b across both bands
reduced_transition_probabilities: B(E2)_out/B(E2)_in = 0.22 - 0.36; B(M1)_out/B(E2)_in = 0.01 - 0.08 (mu_N/eb)^2; absolute B(E2)_in ~ 2.0 e^2 b^2 (superdeformed collective strength!)
branching_and_angular_ratios: 43/2+->41/2+ transition: mixing ratio delta = -3.10(+0.36/-0.44), branching lambda = 0.36(4), establishing 90.6(13)% E2 and 9.4(13)% M1 purity (rejected delta=-0.22 via linear polarization)
citation_primary: S.W. Ødegård et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 86, 5866 (2001); D.R. Jensen et al., PRL 89, 142503 (2002); G. Schönwaßer et al., PLB 552, 9 (2003)
citation_locators: PRL 86, 5866: p. 2 Fig. 1 (level scheme), p. 3 Fig. 3 (alignment and J(2)), p. 4 Fig. 5 (B(E2)_out/B(E2)_in), p. 4 Table I (mixing ratio and branching)
direct_experimental_observable: Prompt 3D/4D coincidence events (2.4 x 10^9 events), DCO ratios, angular distribution ratios, and clover Compton linear polarization
derived_physical_quantity: Multipole mixing ratio delta = -3.10(+0.36/-0.44), B(E2)_out/B(E2)_in, transition quadrupole moment Q_t = 10.7(7) e b, triaxial deformation (epsilon2=0.38, gamma=+20 deg)
model_dependent_interpretation: Triaxial Particle-Rotor Model (Hamamoto & Mottelson): TSD2 is a one-phonon (n_w=1) transverse wobbler; TSD3 is two-phonon (n_w=2) wobbler; collective core wobbles around the intermediate axis
competing_explanations_and_limits: Cranking-like signature partner prediction gives B(E2)_out/B(E2)_in ~ 0.02 (ruled out by a factor of 15!). True wobbling confirmed by both large interband E2 strength and large triaxial superdeformation

physical_mechanism: Systematic candidate for wobbling; example of unconfirmed classification due to missing electromagnetic observables
experimental_facility: EUROBALL IV array at Vivitron accelerator, IReS Strasbourg
lifetime_technique: None (statistics insufficient for DSAM lineshape or RDDS plunger)
level_energies_E_I_keV: TSD1 extended by 6 transitions; TSD2 placed ~650 keV above TSD1; absolute spins tentative
transition_energies_E_gamma_keV: TSD1 in-band transitions: 750 to 1250 keV; connecting transitions tentatively identified in coincidence spectra
reduced_transition_probabilities: Unknown (no absolute or relative B(E2)/B(M1) values measured)
branching_and_angular_ratios: Population intensities: TSD1 ~ 1.4%, TSD2 ~ 0.6% of 161Lu reaction channel; DCO and polarization could not be extracted
citation_primary: P. Bringel et al., Eur. Phys. J. A 24, 167 (2005)
citation_locators: EPJ A 24, 167: pp. 168-170 Figs. 1-3 (spectra & scheme), p. 171 Figs. 5-8 (alignments & dynamic inertia)
direct_experimental_observable: Multi-fold coincidence gamma-ray spectra from 2.8 x 10^9 presorted events
derived_physical_quantity: Dynamic moment of inertia J(2) and quasiparticle alignment ix similar to 163,165,167Lu TSD bands
model_dependent_interpretation: Authors suggest TSD2 is an n_w=1 wobbling excitation based strictly on isotopic systematics with 163,165Lu
competing_explanations_and_limits: Authors explicitly state that electromagnetic properties (delta, polarization, lifetimes) could NOT be determined; remains a 'candidate' rather than confirmed wobbler. Demonstrates the boundary where structural analogy cannot substitute for transition strength proof!

physical_mechanism: Classic rigid axially-symmetric prolate collective rotation (control benchmark against wobbling and shears)
experimental_facility: Multiple facilities (Coulomb excitation and gamma-decay compilations, NNDC/ENSDF)
reaction: Coulomb excitation and in-beam fusion evaporation
lifetime_technique: Direct electronic timing and Coulomb excitation cross sections
level_lifetimes_tau: 2+ state: tau = 2.91(3) ns (T1/2 = 2.02(2) ns); 4+ state: tau = 153(5) ps; 6+ state: tau = 21(1) ps
reduced_transition_probabilities: B(E2; 0+->2+) = 5.06(6) e^2 b^2 (198(2) W.u.); intrinsic quadrupole moment Q_0 = 7.15(5) e b (beta2 = 0.34); B(E2) ratios obey Alaga rotor rules
branching_and_angular_ratios: Pure E2 cascade; energy ratio E(4+)/E(2+) = 3.27, matching the rigid rotor limit of 3.33
citation_primary: S. Raman et al., At. Data Nucl. Data Tables 78, 1 (2001); NNDC Adopted Levels
direct_experimental_observable: Coulomb excitation cross sections, conversion electron lifetimes, delayed coincidence timing
derived_physical_quantity: Intrinsic quadrupole moment Q_0 = 7.15(5) e b, deformation parameter beta2 = 0.34, moments of inertia J(1) ~ 35 hbar^2/MeV
model_dependent_interpretation: Bohr-Mottelson axial rotor: rigid collective rotation perpendicular to the prolate symmetry axis
competing_explanations_and_limits: Benchmark demonstrating the total suppression of wobbling and shears: large prolate deformation (beta2 > 0.3) locks rotation to the collective axis, forbidding planar shears (MR) and forbidding triaxial wobbling (since gamma = 0)

band_or_state: Shears Band 2 (regular Delta I = 1 M1 sequence based on 29/2- bandhead)
physical_mechanism: Magnetic rotation (planar shears mechanism in near-spherical nucleus)
experimental_facility: 88-Inch Cyclotron, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Gammasphere array
reaction: 186W(18O, 5n)199Pb at E_beam = 95 MeV; thick target DSAM
lifetime_technique: DSAM lineshape centroid shift and profile analysis
branching_and_angular_ratios: B(M1)/B(E2) ratios drop from 31(6) to 12(3) (mu_N/eb)^2; R_DCO ~ 0.5 for Delta I=1 dipoles and ~1.0 for crossover Delta I=2 quadrupoles; K-conversion coefficients confirm pure M1 dipoles
citation_primary: R.M. Clark et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 78, 1868 (1997); see also R.M. Clark & A.O. Macchiavelli, Annu. Rev. Nucl. Part. Sci. 50, 1 (2000)
citation_locators: PRL 78, 1868: p. 1869 Fig. 1 (spectra), p. 1870 Fig. 2 (B(M1) vs E_gamma), p. 1870 Fig. 3 (TAC calculation); Clark 2000 p. 7 Fig. 2 (case study)
direct_experimental_observable: High-fold Doppler lineshapes at Gammasphere angles, conversion electron coefficients alpha_K, and DCO ratios
derived_physical_quantity: Level lifetimes tau, absolute reduced transition probabilities B(M1) and B(E2), dynamic moment of inertia J(2) ~ 20 hbar^2/MeV
model_dependent_interpretation: Shears mechanism: two high-j blades (proton blade: pi(h9/2 i13/2)11-, neutron blade: nu i13/2^-1, j_nu=6.5 hbar) close as theta decreases from 90 deg to 30 deg; B(M1) propto sin^2(theta_pi) drops as shears close
competing_explanations_and_limits: High-K collective band interpretation fails completely: high-K bands predict nearly constant B(M1) with spin (Clark 2000 Fig. 5), contradicted by the sharp 5-fold drop; small core quadrupole deformation (|epsilon| < 0.1) confirmed by small B(E2)

physical_mechanism: Magnetic rotation with band crossing: reopening of shears blades via quasiparticle alignment
experimental_facility: Gammasphere and 88-Inch Cyclotron; Cologne Plunger (RDM) and thick target (DSAM)
lifetime_technique: Recoil Distance Method (RDM) for low-spin states + DSAM for high-spin states
level_energies_E_I_keV: Cascade spanning spins from 21/2- to 39/2-; band crossing observed at hbar omega ~ 0.28 MeV (I ~ 31/2- to 33/2-)
transition_energies_E_gamma_keV: Regular M1 cascade: 180 keV, 240 keV, 310 keV, 380 keV, 432 keV, 520 keV
level_lifetimes_tau: Lifetimes measured via RDM (tau ~ 2 to 10 ps at low spin) and DSAM (tau ~ 0.1 to 1 ps at high spin)
reduced_transition_probabilities: B(M1) drops from ~2.2 mu_N^2 to ~0.8 mu_N^2 below crossing, then jumps abruptly back up to ~1.8 mu_N^2 after alignment of an additional i13/2 neutron pair, before decreasing again
branching_and_angular_ratios: 432 keV line polarization measured by Schmid 1998 (NIM A 422, 95) with Gammasphere segmented clover; DCO ratios R_DCO ~ 0.5
citation_primary: E.F. Moore et al., Phys. Rev. C 63, 024303 (2001); R.M. Clark et al., Phys. Lett. B 275, 247 (1992); H. Hübel, PPNP 54, 1 (2005)
citation_locators: PRC 63, 024303: p. 3 Table I (RDM lifetimes), p. 5 Fig. 4 (B(M1) vs spin); Hubel 2005 p. 27 Fig. 23 (B(M1) crossing)
direct_experimental_observable: Plunger decay curves (shifted/unshifted fractions) at low spin; DSAM profiles at high spin; Compton linear polarization
derived_physical_quantity: Level lifetimes tau, B(M1) evolution displaying non-monotonic jump at alignment, dynamic inertia J(2)
model_dependent_interpretation: Shears mechanism with configuration crossing: initial shears pi(h9/2 i13/2) (x) nu i13/2^-1 closes, followed by alignment of a pair of i13/2 neutrons forming a 5-quasiparticle blade that reopens the shears angle
competing_explanations_and_limits: Demonstrates that naive extrapolation of monotonic B(M1) decrease fails when quasiparticle alignments occur; blade lengths and configurations must be tracked dynamically across crossings

band_or_state: Shears band based on odd-odd proton-particle neutron-hole coupling
physical_mechanism: Magnetic rotation in odd-odd nucleus without collective core rotation
lifetime_technique: DSAM lineshape estimates and branching systematics
level_energies_E_I_keV: Cascade extending over 10 transitions from I ~ 15 to 25; regular Delta I=1 ladder
level_lifetimes_tau: Sub-picosecond effective lifetimes inferred from DSAM feeding limits (tau < 0.5 ps)
reduced_transition_probabilities: Enhanced B(M1) ~ 1.5 - 3.0 mu_N^2; very weak cross-over E2 transitions (B(E2) < 0.05 e^2 b^2)
branching_and_angular_ratios: B(M1)/B(E2) ~ 30 - 60 (mu_N/eb)^2; DCO ratios confirm dipole character
citation_primary: R.M. Clark et al., Phys. Rev. C 50, 84 (1994); H. Hübel, Prog. Part. Nucl. Phys. 54, 1 (2005)
citation_locators: PRC 50, 84: p. 85 Fig. 1 (spectra), p. 86 Fig. 2 (level scheme); Hubel 2005 p. 13 Table 1
direct_experimental_observable: Prompt coincidence gamma cascades, DCO ratios, and transition intensity branching
derived_physical_quantity: Kinematic and dynamic moments of inertia J(1), J(2); B(M1)/B(E2) ratios

experimental_facility: CERN ISOLDE, REX-ISOLDE post-accelerator, MINIBALL germanium detector array

lifetime_technique: Multi-step Coulomb excitation cross-section analysis using GOSIA code (model-independent electromagnetic matrix extraction)

reduced_transition_probabilities: Direct E3: <3-||M(E3)||0+> = 0.94(3) e b^(3/2), B(E3; 0+->3-) = 42(3) W.u.; intrinsic octupole moment Q_30 = 2520(90) e fm^3; transition quadrupole moment Q_20 = 640(10) e fm^2
branching_and_angular_ratios: Alternating parity sequence with energy displacement delta E(I) = E(I-) - [E((I+1)+) + E((I-1)+)]/2 rapidly approaching zero; multiple E1, E2, E3 Coulex cross sections fitted simultaneously
citation_primary: L.P. Gaffney et al., Nature 497, 199 (2013); P.A. Butler et al., Nat. Commun. 10, 2473 (2019); P.A. Butler et al., PRL 124, 042503 (2020)

derived_physical_quantity: Transitional and diagonal matrix elements <I_f||M(E lambda)||I_i> extracted via GOSIA; intrinsic octupole moment Q_30 = 2520(90) e fm^3; intrinsic quadrupole moment Q_20 = 640(10) e fm^2
model_dependent_interpretation: Permanent intrinsic reflection-asymmetric octupole deformation (stable pear shape) arising from proton pi(f7/2 <-> i13/2) and neutron nu(g9/2 <-> j15/2) coupling
competing_explanations_and_limits: Octupole vibration vs static deformation: Gaffney 2013 proved that 224Ra possesses a static pear shape because Q_30 remains constant across spins and B(E3) is massive (42 W.u.), in contrast to 220Rn which is an octupole vibrator (Q_30 increases with spin)

physical_mechanism: Octupole deformation in actinide nucleus; parity doublet structure

competing_explanations_and_limits: Crucial cross-mass warning: Proves that E1 strength CANNOT be used as a proxy for octupole deformation!
